content: localStorage/sessionStorage are fully readable by any JS running on the page, so a single XSS vulnerability can exfiltrate all stored secrets/keys. In-memory (JS variable) storage is somewhat harder to exfiltrate than persistent storage but does NOT solve the problem -- if XSS exists, the frontend must be considered fully compromised. The correct primary defense is rigorous XSS prevention (CSP, output encoding, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML/eval), not the choice of storage location.
